'''The Young Turks''' (TYT) is an American progressive news and commentary network, one of the earliest and largest online political shows, founded by '''Cenk Uygur''' and long co-anchored with '''Ana Kasparian'''. It appears in [[Media and Personalities]] among the cable-and-commentary outlets, read for its real history and its strong and weak cases — and connected to our political coverage in [[SoapBox Politics]].

== The real history ==

TYT began as a talk-radio show in 2002 and moved early and aggressively onto the internet, becoming a pioneer of long-form online political commentary years before "YouTube news" was a category. It built a very large audience on a simple proposition: progressive, unfiltered commentary outside the corporate-media gatekeepers, delivered daily and at length. That first-mover position — proving an audience existed for independent political media — is a large part of why it matters.

== What it is ==

The network pairs a flagship news-commentary show with a stable of spin-offs and reporters, arguing a broadly progressive, anti-corporate line: campaign-finance reform, labor and economic populism, criticism of both Republican politics and of the Democratic establishment from the left, and sustained critique of how legacy media covers (or ignores) those stories.

== The strong case ==

TYT helped build the independent-media ecosystem this whole section studies: it showed that online political media could reach and sustain mass audiences, it has done real original reporting and advocacy on money-in-politics and labor, and it regularly surfaces stories the cable nets underplay. Its willingness to criticize its ''own'' side — the Democratic establishment — distinguishes it from pure partisan media.

== The weak case ==

It also carries the failure modes of the outrage-driven commentary format: a pull toward sensationalism and hot takes, episodes of being loose with framing or facts, and recurring internal and public controversies — including Cenk Uygur's own early-2000s writings, which he has since disavowed and apologized for. Treat it as an engaged, partisan-progressive commentary source with a real reporting streak, not a neutral newswire — and read its claims against the record in [[SoapBox Politics]] and [[SoapBox Oversight]].
